# Introduction

Build on Tempest Core and the Tempest plugins for Hytale.

The Tempest plugins can be used from other plugins (Java) and from content mods that have no code (JSON assets). **Core** is the base: everything shared is in `com.atomictempest.core`
(events, leaderboards, help, settings, HUD lines, perks, and the economy bridge). Each plugin has its own small `api`
package.

| Plugin | Manifest id | API |
|---|---|---|
| Core | `AtomicTempest:Core` | `com.atomictempest.core` (`economy.Economies`, events, leaderboards, help, settings, HUD lines, perks) |
| Coins | `AtomicTempest:Coins` | `com.atomictempest.coins.api.CoinsAPI` (what only Coins has), `CoinStacks` |
| Quests | `AtomicTempest:Quests` | `com.atomictempest.quests.api.QuestsAPI` |
| Lottery | `AtomicTempest:Lottery` | `com.atomictempest.lottery.api.LotteryAPI` |
| SlotMachine | `AtomicTempest:SlotMachine` | `com.atomictempest.slotmachine.api.SlotMachineAPI` |
| Shop | `AtomicTempest:Shop` | `com.atomictempest.shop.api.ShopAPI` |
| Coinflip | `AtomicTempest:Coinflip` | `com.atomictempest.coinflip.api.CoinflipAPI`, `RoomMode` |
| Events | `AtomicTempest:Events` | no API of its own: it turns on Core's `Boosts` (below) and has placeholders |
| Contracts | `AtomicTempest:Contracts` | no API of its own: the `contract_deliver` action, the `contract_pay` boost kind and placeholders |
| Projects | `AtomicTempest:Projects` | `com.atomictempest.projects.api.ProjectsAPI` (the buildings and their states); the `projects_donate` action (amount: items given), `projects_coins` (amount: coins given) and the `projects_open` placeholder |
| Town | `AtomicTempest:Town` | no API of its own: it decides Core's `Unlocks` (below), and has the `town_unlocked`, `town_total` and `town_mayor` placeholders |
| Crates | `AtomicTempest:Crates` | no API of its own: the `crate_open` action and `Announcements.BIG_WIN` |
| Holograms | `AtomicTempest:Holograms` | `com.atomictempest.holograms.api.Holograms` (and `Hologram`, `TextArt`, `Rankings`...) |
| Pass | `AtomicTempest:Pass` | `com.atomictempest.pass.api.PassAPI` |
| Jobs | `AtomicTempest:Jobs` | `com.atomictempest.jobs.api.JobsAPI` |
| Trade | `AtomicTempest:Trade` | no API of its own: the `trade_done` action |

With **Endless Leveling** or **MMO Skill Tree** installed, Core's `Levels` and `Skills` give every plugin player
levels, skills and what happens in them, without depending on either mod.

Every API class has a version constant that goes up when something is added. Everything in these APIs is safe to call
from any thread unless it says otherwise.

**Javadoc:** [Coinflip 1.0.3](javadoc/coinflip/) · [Coins 2.4.0](javadoc/coins/) · [Core 1.5.0](javadoc/core/) · [Holograms 1.2.1](javadoc/holograms/) · [Jobs 1.1.0](javadoc/jobs/) · [Lottery 1.1.2](javadoc/lottery/) · [Pass 1.2.1](javadoc/pass/) · [Projects 1.1.0](javadoc/projects/) · [Quests 1.4.0](javadoc/quests/) · [Shop 1.5.0](javadoc/shop/) · [SlotMachine 1.2.2](javadoc/slotmachine/)

**Jars:** from the plugins' CurseForge pages; compile against them with `compileOnly`. **Questions and help:** [Discord](https://discord.gg/Q9PNVCMZXK)


# Quick start

From an empty plugin to one that pays players and reads their level, in five steps.

## Checklist

| Step | What to do |
|---|---|
| 1 | Put Tempest Core (and the plugins you use) in your server's `mods` folder, and compile against their jars with `compileOnly` |
| 2 | Depend on `AtomicTempest:Core` in your `manifest.json`; make the other Tempest plugins optional |
| 3 | Make one `Registrations` for your plugin and `close()` it in `shutdown()` |
| 4 | Ask Core for what you need on every use (`Economies.get()`, `Levels.get()`): mods can start after yours |
| 5 | Before using anything newer than the Core you support, check `CoreAPI.runningVersion()` |

## 1. Compile against the jars

Download the jars from the plugins' CurseForge pages, then in `build.gradle`:

```groovy
dependencies {
    compileOnly(files("libs/Core-1.5.0.jar"))
    compileOnly(files("libs/Quests-1.4.0.jar"))   // only if you use it
}
```

`compileOnly` means the jars are not packed into yours: the server loads them from its `mods` folder.

## 2. Declare the dependencies

```json
"Dependencies": { "AtomicTempest:Core": "*" },
"OptionalDependencies": { "AtomicTempest:Coins": "*", "AtomicTempest:Quests": "*" }
```

> **Note:** With an optional dependency, check that the plugin is there (`QuestsAPI.isAvailable()`,
> `CoinsAPI.get() != null`) and touch its classes in one class of yours only, so your plugin still loads without it.

## 3. Register with Core

```java
public class DragonsPlugin extends JavaPlugin {
    private final Registrations core = new Registrations("Dragons");

    public DragonsPlugin(JavaPluginInit init) {
        super(init);
    }

    @Override
    protected void setup() {
        core.placeholder("dragons_slain", uuid -> String.valueOf(slain(uuid)));
        core.onAction((player, action, amount) -> {
            if (action.equals(PlayerActions.CRATE_OPEN)) { /* a crate was opened */ }
        });
    }

    @Override
    public void shutdown() {
        core.close();   // takes back everything registered above
        super.shutdown();
    }
}
```

## 4. Pay a player, read their level

```java
Economy money = Economies.get();                     // null while no economy is installed
if (money != null) {
    money.deposit(player, 250, "Dragons: a dragon slain");   // the reason shows in the economy log
}

Levels.Leveling leveling = Levels.get();             // Endless Leveling or MMO Skill Tree, or null
if (leveling != null && leveling.level(player) >= 20) {
    leveling.giveXp(player, 100, "Dragons: a dragon slain");
}
```

## 5. Check the Core version

```java
if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 19 && Skills.available()) {
    int mining = Skills.level(player, "Mining");     // MMO Skill Tree skills (API 19)
}
```

> **Tip:** Keep code that needs a newer Core in a class of its own and call it only after the check: on an older Core
> the class is then never loaded, and your plugin keeps working.

Next: [Setting up a plugin](setup.html) has every option, and [Player actions](actions.html) lists everything the
Tempest plugins report.


# Setting up a plugin

Dependencies, Registrations, config files and which Core is installed.

## Setting up a plugin

1. Compile against the jars you use, without bundling them; the server loads them from Mods:

   ```groovy
   dependencies {
       compileOnly(files("$hytaleHome/UserData/Mods/Core-1.0.0.jar"))
       compileOnly(files("$hytaleHome/UserData/Mods/Quests-1.1.0.jar"))   // only if you use it
   }
   ```

   Download the jars from the plugins' CurseForge pages (https://www.curseforge.com/hytale/mods/search?search=tempest).

2. In your `manifest.json`, depend on what you use so it starts before your plugin:

   ```json
   "Dependencies": { "AtomicTempest:Core": "*" },
   "OptionalDependencies": { "AtomicTempest:Coins": "*", "AtomicTempest:Quests": "*" }
   ```

   With an optional dependency, check `CoinsAPI.get() != null` or `QuestsAPI.isAvailable()` (or
   `LotteryAPI.isAvailable()` ...) before use, and keep the classes that touch it apart from the rest, so your plugin
   still loads when it is missing.

3. Use the APIs in your plugin's `setup()` or later.

### The shortest way: `Registrations` and `JsonFiles` (Core)

`Registrations` registers with Core's registries and remembers how to undo each one; one `close()` in `shutdown()`
takes it all back, so a reload never leaves a settings tab, help page, listener or timer behind:

```java
private final Registrations core = new Registrations("Dragons");

protected void setup() {
    config = DragonsConfig.load();
    core.settingsTab(new SettingsTab("Dragons", settings(config), config::save));
    core.helpTopic(new HelpTopic("dragons", 80, Message.translation("server.dragons.help.title"), "Rock_Gem_Ruby", uuid -> lines(uuid)));
    core.helpCommand("server.dragons.help.mod", "/dragons", Message.translation("server.dragons.help.command"));
    core.hudLine("dragons.next", uuid -> Message.translation("server.dragons.hud.next"));
    core.placeholder("dragons_slain", uuid -> String.valueOf(slain(uuid)));
    core.mapKind(new MapPlaces.Kind("nest", "Dragon nests", Message.translation("server.dragons.map.nest")).blocks("Dragon_Nest"::equals));
    core.leaderboard(board);  core.onWallet(listener);  core.veto(veto);  core.onAction(listener);
    core.onAnnouncement(listener);  core.restrictCraft("Dragon_Egg", () -> config.playersCanCraft());
    core.edition(isPro, PRO_ADDS, licensedTo);     // plugins with a free and a Pro jar
    core.every(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS, () -> spawnDragons());        // its own daemon timer thread; errors are logged
    core.later(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS, () -> greet());
    core.onClose(() -> config.save());                             // anything else for shutdown()
}

public void shutdown() {
    core.close();                                                  // newest first; calling it twice does nothing
    super.shutdown();
}
```

`JsonFiles` loads and saves a config or data file with `SafeFiles` (crash-safe) and Gson, pretty-printed. Fields the
file does not have keep the class's defaults, so new settings never break old files:

```java
static DragonsConfig load() { return JsonFiles.loadAndSave(PATH, DragonsConfig.class, DragonsConfig::new); }
void save() { JsonFiles.save(PATH, this); }
Map<String, Long> times = JsonFiles.load(PATH, new TypeToken<Map<String, Long>>() {}.getType(), HashMap::new);
```

A setting renamed or moved later keeps the server's value with config versions (API 12): give the class an
`int configVersion` field and list the steps; a file runs only the steps it has not had yet.

```java
JsonFiles.loadAndSave(PATH, DragonsConfig.class, DragonsConfig::new, List.of(
        json -> JsonFiles.rename(json, "dragonsPerHour", "spawnsPerHour")));     // version 1
```


## Which Core is installed: `CoreAPI` (Core)

`CoreAPI.runningVersion()` is the API version of the Core on the server (`CoreAPI.API_VERSION` is the one you
compiled against; it is copied into your plugin, so ask `runningVersion()` at run time). Version 1 is Core 1.0.0.

Core's **stable API**, safe to build on: the classes directly in `com.atomictempest.core` (except `Main`) and the
packages `economy`, `help` and `settings`. These only grow. Core's `command`, `config`, `listener`, `player` and `ui`
packages and `Main` are internal and may change in any release; do not use them. The other plugins' APIs are their
`api` packages (`Holograms.API_VERSION`, `QuestsAPI.API_VERSION`, `CoinsAPI.VERSION`, `CoinflipAPI.VERSION` ...).

```java
if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() < 1) { /* a Core older than the one you built against */ }
```


# API versions

What each Core API version added, to check before you use it.

## Reference: Core API versions

`CoreAPI.API_VERSION` is the version a plugin was built against; `CoreAPI.runningVersion()` is the one installed on
the server. Check the running version before touching anything newer than your lowest supported Core, and keep that
code in a class of its own.

| Version | Added |
|---|---|
| 1 | Core 1.0.0: `Registrations`, `JsonFiles`, `Economies`, `CasinoSettings`, `HelpTopics`, `HudLines`, `Leaderboards`, `Placeholders`, `PlayerActions`, `WalletEvents` and the rest of the first release |
| 2 | `AdminLog`, `RateLimit`, and settings tab groups (`tempest.admin.<group>`) |
| 3 | `PlayLimits`, `HudLines.compact`, `Themes`, dropdowns and item pickers in settings (`Setting.choice`, `Setting.item`), tab icons, `ItemIcons.ids` and `pretty` |
| 4 | The Tempest board's line names and keys (`HudLines.name`, `nameOf`, `keys`, `lineFor`) |
| 5 | `Boosts` and `Registrations.boost`; `PlayerActions.QUEST_COMPLETE` and `CONTRACT_DELIVER` |
| 6 | `Mailbox` (/mail) and `HudLines.startOff` |
| 7 | `MapPlaces` and `Registrations.mapKind` |
| 8 | `Unlocks` and `Registrations.unlockFeature`, `unlockProvider`, `onUnlock` |
| 9 | `Activity` and `Perks.highestPercent` |
| 10 | `Perks.Bonus.PASS_XP` |
| 11 | `SettingsTab.defaults` (Reset to defaults) |
| 12 | `JsonFiles` config versions with migrations, and `JsonFiles.rename` |
| 13 | `Doctor` (/tempest doctor) and `Registrations.doctor` |
| 14 | `Levels`: player levels from a leveling mod |
| 15 | `Levels` dungeon, wave gate and raid clears; `Boosts.LEVELING_XP` |
| 16 | `Levels` XP, level cap, class, race, mob level, parties, raid starts, `meets`, `hasClass`, `mobGold`, `mobKilled`, `playersAtLevel`, `serverClears`, `serverPrestige`; `Registrations.levelingTab`, `levelingFeature`; `Unlocks.isUnlocked` |
| 17 | `Demand` and `Registrations.demandSource`; `HudLines.progress` |
| 18 | `Rewards`: item and command rewards the same in every plugin |
| 19 | `Skills` (MMO Skill Tree) and its moments as `PlayerActions`; MMO Skill Tree as a leveling mod next to Endless Leveling; `Registrations.endlessTab`. Comes with Core 1.6.0, the next release |


# Money

The server's economy, whichever plugin keeps it, and what only Tempest Economy (Coins) has.

## Money: `Economies` (Core)

The server's money, whichever plugin keeps it: Coins when it is installed, otherwise any economy VaultUnlocked offers
(Ecotale, TheEconomy, EliteEssentials...). Ask for it on every use: an economy can start after your plugin.

```java
Economy money = Economies.get();                    // com.atomictempest.core.economy; null when there is none

long balance = money.balance(uuid);
money.deposit(uuid, 250, "Dragon bounty");           // false if refused; the reason shows in Coins' wallet history
if (money.withdraw(uuid, 100, "Ferry ticket")) { /* paid */ }   // false (nothing taken) if too little or vetoed
money.has(uuid, 100);
money.format(1250);                                  // "1,250 copper", or "$1,250.00" from another economy
```

Amounts are whole numbers of the economy's smallest unit (an economy with decimals shows balances rounded down).
Always give a reason. `withdraw` asks the `WalletEvents` vetoes first, and every change through any economy reaches
`WalletEvents` listeners. Coins the player holds as items are not in the wallet until deposited.


## Coins: `CoinsAPI`

What only Coins has. `CoinsAPI` is also an `Economy`, so everything above works on it too.

```java
CoinsAPI coins = CoinsAPI.get();                    // null when Coins is not installed

coins.setBalance(uuid, 1000);                        // "Set by an admin" in the history
coins.transfer(from, to, 50, "Trade");               // "Paid: Trade" / "Received: Trade"
coins.paidAsCoins(uuid, 250, "Slot machine win");    // VERSION 4: you paid coin items instead of the wallet
List<ItemStack> items = CoinStacks.of(1250);         // coin items worth an amount, most valuable first
```

When your plugin pays out coin items instead of money (dropped, put in a tray), call `paidAsCoins` with the reason you
would give a wallet change: the balance does not change, but the economy screen (`/eco`) and the leaderboards count
the payout under its kind. Without it the money shows up only later, as "Deposited coins".

**Town unlock:** Coins describes the feature `coins:bank_interest` ("Bank savings interest") with Core's `Unlocks`
(Core API 8) and pays savings interest only while `Unlocks.isOn("coins:bank_interest")` and the admin has switched it
on. A plugin that decides the unlocks (`Registrations.unlockProvider`) can keep it off, for example until a bank
building is finished; without one, Coins' own setting decides. Interest is paid into banks with the history line
"Savings interest" (no wallet changes, so no `WalletEvents`).


## Stopping payments: `WalletEvents.addVeto`

A veto is asked before coins **leave** a wallet (bets, crates, shop purchases, payments) and can refuse with a
sentence for the player. Coins coming in cannot be refused, because the player may already have handed something
over for them.

```java
WalletEvents.addVeto((uuid, amount, reason) -> jail.contains(uuid) ? "You cannot spend coins in jail." : null);
String why = WalletEvents.checkRemoval(uuid, 100, "Ferry ticket");   // ask first to show the reason
```


# Player actions

Hear what players do in every Tempest plugin, and report your own.

All in `com.atomictempest.core`, available whether or not Coins is installed.


## Hearing about money: `WalletEvents` and `PlayerActions`

```java
// Every change of any wallet (after it happened)
WalletEvents.listen((player, amount, reason, balanceAfter) -> { ... });

// What players do in the economy mods: spins, wins, tickets, shop trades, daily rewards, payments
PlayerActions.listen((player, action, amount) -> {
    if (PlayerActions.SLOT_JACKPOT.equals(action)) { ... }
});

// Report your own (other listeners, such as Quests, may count them)
PlayerActions.fire(uuid, "mymod:bounty", 250);
```

Actions: `slot_spin` (bet), `slot_win` (winnings, also when dropped as coins), `slot_jackpot`, `lottery_tickets`
(how many), `lottery_win`, `shop_buy` (cost), `shop_sell` (paid), `daily_reward`, `pay`, `crate_open` (price),
`coinflip_bet` (stake), `coinflip_win` (paid), `coinflip_loss` (stake), `quest_complete` (reward paid; Core API 5,
reported by Quests for every quest and achievement finished), `contract_deliver` (items delivered; Core API 5, reported by
Contracts for every delivery to a server order), `events_top` (the place, 1 to 3, when an event ends), `events_helped`
(a goal reached and the helper paid), `trade_done` (to each side of a finished trade that moved something; the amount is
a number that always stands for the same other player), `town_mayor` (elected at the end of a term).

Listeners run on the thread that made the change: keep them quick, and do world or UI work with `world.execute(...)`.


## Reference: every player action

Everything the Tempest plugins report through `PlayerActions` (Core), in one place. Listen once and count what you
need; the amount means what the table says. Listeners run on the thread that reported: keep them quick and
thread-safe.

```java
PlayerActions.listen((player, action, amount) -> {
    switch (action) {
        case PlayerActions.CRATE_OPEN -> ...;     // a constant on PlayerActions
        case "jobs_level" -> ...;                 // the other plugins' actions are plain strings
        default -> { }
    }
});
```

| Action | From | Fires when | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot_spin` (`PlayerActions.SLOT_SPIN`) | Slots | A slot machine spin | The bet |
| `slot_win` (`SLOT_WIN`) | Slots | A win, paid or dropped as coins | The winnings |
| `slot_jackpot` (`SLOT_JACKPOT`) | Slots | A jackpot (also reported as a win) | The winnings |
| `lottery_tickets` (`LOTTERY_TICKETS`) | Lottery | Tickets bought | How many |
| `lottery_win` (`LOTTERY_WIN`) | Lottery | A lottery win | The prize |
| `shop_buy` (`SHOP_BUY`) | Shop | Bought from the shop | What it cost |
| `shop_sell` (`SHOP_SELL`) | Shop | Sold to the shop | What it paid |
| `daily_reward` (`DAILY_REWARD`) | Coins | A daily reward claimed | The reward |
| `pay` (`PAY`) | Coins | A payment to another player | What was paid |
| `crate_open` (`CRATE_OPEN`) | Crates | A crate opened | What it cost (0 when free) |
| `quest_complete` (`QUEST_COMPLETE`, API 5) | Quests | A quest or achievement finished | The reward paid, 0 if none |
| `contract_deliver` (`CONTRACT_DELIVER`, API 5) | Contracts | Items delivered to a contract or server order | How many items |
| `coinflip_bet` (`CoinflipAPI.ACTION_BET`) | Coinflip | A stake put into a room | The stake |
| `coinflip_win` (`CoinflipAPI.ACTION_WIN`) | Coinflip | A flip won | The payout |
| `coinflip_loss` (`CoinflipAPI.ACTION_LOSS`) | Coinflip | A flip lost | The stake |
| `jobs_paid` | Jobs | Pay for job work | What was paid |
| `jobs_level` | Jobs | A job level reached | The level |
| `jobs_tree` | Jobs | A whole tree felled as a woodcutter | 1 |
| `jobs_found` | Jobs | A new place found as an explorer | 1 |
| `events_top` | Events | Finished in an event's top three | The place (1 to 3) |
| `events_helped` | Events | Helped enough when a goal (or overdrive stage) was reached | 1 |
| `projects_donate` | Projects | Items given to a town project | How many items |
| `projects_coins` | Projects | Coins given to a town project | The coins |
| `trade_done` | Trade | A finished trade that moved something (to both sides) | A number that stands for the other player, the same every time |
| `town_mayor` | Town | Elected mayor (not set by an admin) | 1 |
| `mmo_skill_level:<id> <name>` (`Skills.SKILL_LEVEL`, API 19) | Core, with MMO Skill Tree | A skill's level went up | The new level |
| `mmo_skill_xp:<id> <name>` (`Skills.SKILL_XP`, API 19) | Core, with MMO Skill Tree | Skill XP from play | The XP |
| `mmo_achievement:<id>` (`Skills.ACHIEVEMENT`, API 19) | Core, with MMO Skill Tree | An achievement unlocked | 1 |
| `mmo_quest:<id>` (`Skills.QUEST`, API 19) | Core, with MMO Skill Tree | One of its quests finished | 1 |
| `npc_talk:<character id> <aliases>` (`Skills.NPC_TALK`, API 19) | Core, with MMO Skill Tree | A credited conversation with a character | 1 |

> **Tip:** Your own plugin can report actions too: `PlayerActions.fire(player, "mymod_dragon_slain", 1)`. Use a
> prefix of your own so names never clash; Tempest Quests' custom triggers can count them.


# Settings and menus

A /tempest settings tab for your plugin, menu themes, editions, languages and help pages.

## Admin settings: `CasinoSettings`

```java
CasinoSettings.register(new SettingsTab("Dragons", List.of(
        Setting.heading("Bounties", "What players earn for dragons."),
        Setting.number("Bounty", 0, 1_000_000, 0, () -> config.bounty, v -> config.bounty = (long) v)
                .hint("Per dragon.").preview(() -> Message.raw("= " + Currency.format(config.bounty))),
        Setting.toggle("Announce kills", () -> config.announce, v -> config.announce = v),
        Setting.text("Chat tag", true, () -> config.tag, v -> config.tag = v).icon("Weapon_Sword_Iron").caption("Tag"),
        Setting.color("Colour", () -> config.tagColor, v -> config.tagColor = v).inline()
), config::save));
```

Your tab appears in `/tempest` for admins (permission `tempest.admin`), up to 40 settings. Staff with
`tempest.admin.<group>` see only that group's tabs. The group is the title in lower case without spaces
(`tempest.admin.dragons`); give it yourself when your plugin has more than one tab, so one permission covers them all
(API 2): `new SettingsTab("Dragon Loot", "dragons", settings, config::save)`.

Where there are only a few right answers, give admins a dropdown instead of a number or a code (API 3):

```java
Setting.choice("Difficulty", List.of(Setting.option("easy", "Easy"), Setting.option("hard", "Hard")),
        () -> config.difficulty, v -> config.difficulty = v),
Setting.choiceNumber("Corner", List.of(Setting.option("1", "Top right"), Setting.option("2", "Left")),
        () -> config.corner, v -> config.corner = v),             // a setting kept as a whole number
Setting.item("Reward item", () -> config.item, v -> config.item = v),   // every item, with a search box
Setting.choice("Crate", () -> crateChoices(), true, () -> config.crate, v -> config.crate = v)  // worked out each time
```

A dropdown only saves one of its own entries. Give your tab an icon for the menu's side bar (API 3):
`new SettingsTab("Dragons", settings, config::save).icon("Weapon_Sword_Iron")`. The side bar lists Core's tabs, then
plugins with several tabs under their name, then the rest under "Plugins".

A Reset to defaults button (API 11): give the tab the same settings built on a fresh config. An admin clicks it twice,
every value is copied over, logged and saved through your save action. Guard it for older Cores:

```java
SettingsTab tab = new SettingsTab("Dragons", settings(config), config::save);
if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 11) {
    tab.defaults(() -> settings(new DragonsConfig()));
}
```


## Menu themes: `Themes` (API version 3)

The admin picks the look of every Tempest menu (`/tempest`, General, "Menu theme"): Tempest gold (the plugins' own
look), Dark crimson, Elven emerald, Frostbite, Amethyst, Cyberpunk neon, Cozy parchment, or their own two colours.
Use it on your pages so they match:

Put your `.ui` files in a folder with your own name in it (`Common/UI/Custom/Pages/MyName_Dragons/`), never straight
in `Pages/` or in a folder named after a feature (`Pages/Quests/`): every mod's UI files and the game's share one
folder tree in the client, and a file at the same path as another mod's replaces it. Tempest's own are in
`Pages/AtomicTempest_<Plugin>/` and `Hud/AtomicTempest_*`.

```java
cmd.append("Pages/MyName_Dragons/DragonsPage.ui");
Themes.tint(cmd, "#Content");                            // the page's body in the theme's colour
cmd.set("#Heading.TextSpans", Themes.accent("Bounties")); // titles and highlights
Themes.row(cmd, "#List[0]");                             // a row in the theme's row colour
```

The default theme paints nothing, so a page looks as its `.ui` file says until an admin picks a theme.


## Free and Pro editions: `Editions`

For plugins that come as a free and a Pro jar (Crates, Quests and Holograms do; yours can too). Register the edition
in `setup()`, unregister it in `shutdown()`. Only admins ever see these texts.

```java
Editions.register("MyPlugin", isPro, List.of("any number of arenas", "team modes"), licensedTo);
settings.add(Editions.heading("MyPlugin"));          // "Free edition: the Pro edition adds ..." at the end of your /tempest tab
String why = Editions.limitReached("MyPlugin", "5 arenas"); // "The free edition of MyPlugin has up to 5 arenas. ..."
String what = Editions.proOnly("MyPlugin", "Team modes");   // "Team modes are in the Pro edition of MyPlugin."
Editions.isPro("Crates");                            // which edition another plugin runs
```

`licensedTo` is shown in the Pro heading ("Licensed to ..."); pass "" when there is none. Keep your API the same in both
editions, and let free limits only stop making more, never break what a server already has.


## Languages: `Lang`

Texts are Hytale translation keys. Put them in `src/main/resources/Server/Languages/<locale>/server.lang` (prefix them with
your plugin's id, so `mymod.help.title = Dragons` is `server.mymod.help.title`), set `"IncludesAssetPack": true`, and
send `Message.translation(key).param(...)`. The game fills in English for keys a language lacks. `Message.raw(text)`
still works for text that needs no translation.

```java
String language = Lang.languageOf(playerRef);                  // the language the plugins use for this player
String text = Lang.text(language, Message.translation("server.mymod.hud.bounty").param("amount", "250")); // for logs, signs, placeholders
```

The admin can pick one language for everyone (`/tempest` → General → Language), for languages Hytale does not offer
yet (German, Italian, Polish). That only covers keys under the Tempest plugins' own prefixes.


## The help screen: `HelpTopics`

```java
HelpTopics.register(new HelpTopic("mymod", 80, Message.translation("server.mymod.help.title"), "Weapon_Sword_Iron",
                uuid -> List.of(
                        HelpTopic.heading("server.mymod.help.bounties"),
                        Message.translation("server.mymod.help.earn").param("amount", Currency.format(250))))
        .button(Message.translation("server.mymod.help.open"), (player, ref, store) -> { openPage(player, ref, store); return false; }));
HelpTopics.registerCommand("server.mymod.help.mod", "/bounties", Message.translation("server.mymod.help.bountiesCmd"));
```

`HelpTopics.open(playerRef, ref, store)` opens the help screen (for a command like `/coins`).
`HelpTopics.justWelcomed(uuid)` is true for a minute after the help screen opened by itself for a new player: a page you
would open on join should wait, so the two do not cover each other.

`HelpTopic.heading(key)` makes a heading line (bold). Shown in `/guide` (and `/coins` with Coins) for every player.


# Boards, HUD and placeholders

Leaderboards, the money counter and progress bars, placeholders and announcements.

## Leaderboards: `Leaderboards`

Shown on Coins' `/leaderboards` (servers without Coins have no leaderboard screen; registering is still safe).

```java
Leaderboards.register(new Leaderboards.Board("mymod:dragons", Message.translation("server.mymod.board.title"),
        Message.translation("server.mymod.board.hint"), "server.mymod.board.count", uuid -> MyMod.dragonsKilled(uuid)));
// count key: a number with its unit, "{count, plural, one {1 dragon} other {{count} dragons}}"; null = money ("1,250 copper")
```

The board appears on `/leaderboards` after the built-in ones. It ranks every player Coins knows; players with 0 are
left out. Unregister it in your `shutdown()`.


## The coin counter: `HudLines`

```java
HudLines.register("mymod:bounty", uuid -> hasBounty(uuid)
        ? Message.translation("server.mymod.hud.bounty").param("amount", HudLines.format(bounty(uuid))) : null);
```

Up to three lines show under each player's coin counter; return null to show nothing. Called every two seconds from a
timer thread. With the Tempest board on (Core's panel on the right of the screen), every line shows there instead, and
each player picks which ones in `/board`. Give your line a name for that menu (API version 4):

```java
HudLines.name("mymod:bounty", Message.translation("server.mymod.board.bounty"));   // "Bounty"
HudLines.keys();  HudLines.nameOf(key);  HudLines.lineFor(key, uuid);              // API version 4
```

A line that is nice to have but should not push others off a full board can start off; each player switches it on in
`/board` (API version 6; Shop's daily deal does this):

```java
if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 6) HudLines.startOff("mymod:bounty");
```

An economy plugin calls `HudLines.moneyChanged(player, change)` when a balance changes, so the counter shows the new
amount and the change at once instead of at its next refresh, and `HudLines.refreshMoney()` after the currency's name or
look changed (Coins does both).


## A progress bar on the screen: `HudLines.progress` (Core, API version 17)

A bar under the money counter for five seconds: an item icon, a short line and how far along (0 to 1). A newer bar
replaces the one showing. Shown even while the Tempest board replaces the counter, never when the player hid it with
/hud. One HUD for everything, so it never fights another mod's HUD.

```java
HudLines.progress(uuid, "Tool_Pickaxe_Iron", Message.raw("Miner 14   +6 XP"), 0.42f);
HudLines.progress(uuid, "Tool_Pickaxe_Iron", Message.raw("Miner 14"), 0.42f, 8000);   // shown for 8 seconds
```


## Placeholders: `Placeholders`

Named values per player, for scoreboards, chat formats and placeholder plugins:

```java
Placeholders.value(uuid, "coins_balance_formatted");             // "1,250 copper"
Placeholders.apply(uuid, "Balance: {coins_balance_formatted}");    // {name} and %name% both work
Placeholders.register("mymod_bounty", uuid -> String.valueOf(bounty(uuid)));
```

| Placeholder | From | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `money_balance`, `money_balance_formatted`, `money_balance_short`, `money_perk` | Core (any economy) | `1250`, `1,250 copper`, `12.5K`, `VIP` |
| `coins_balance`, `coins_balance_formatted`, `coins_balance_short` | Coins | `1250`, `1,250 copper`, `1,250` |
| `coins_currency`, `coins_rank`, `coins_daily_streak`, `coins_daily_ready` | Coins | `copper`, `3`, `5`, `yes` |
| `lottery_pot`, `lottery_pot_raw`, `lottery_time_left`, `lottery_ticket_price`, `lottery_tickets` | Lottery | `5,000 copper`, `12 minutes`, `3` |
| `slots_jackpot`, `slots_jackpot_raw`, `slots_bet` | SlotMachine | `2,400 copper`, `50 copper` |
| `achievements_unlocked`, `achievements_total`, `quests_active`, `quests_current`, `quests_points`, `quests_rank`, `quests_streak` | Quests | `7`, `19`, `2`, `Daily miner  40%`, `230`, `Adventurer`, `3` |
| `coinflip_wins`, `coinflip_losses`, `coinflip_profit`, `coinflip_profit_formatted`, `coinflip_staked`, `coinflip_rooms` | Coinflip | `12`, `9`, `850`, `850 copper`, `4000`, `3` |
| `events_name`, `events_time_left`, `events_goal_percent`, `events_next` | Events | `Gold Rush`, `1h 5m`, `42`, `Monster Hunt` (empty when nothing is on) |
| `contracts_delivered`, `contracts_earned`, `contracts_earned_formatted`, `contracts_rank`, `contracts_open`, `contracts_to_collect`, `contracts_market_items`, `contracts_sold`, `contracts_bounty`, `contracts_bounties_claimed`, `contracts_most_wanted` | Contracts | `120`, `540`, `540 copper`, `Courier`, `7`, `10`, `14`, `320` |
| `events_fund_percent`, `events_fund_total`, `events_stage` | Events | `42`, `10500`, `2` (empty when the fund is off or nothing is on) |
| `town_unlocked`, `town_total`, `town_mayor` | Town | `3`, `5`, `Steve` |


## Announcements: `Announcements`

Big moments (jackpots, big wins, lottery winners, achievements) are posted here for integrations such as the Discord
webhook. Post your own: `Announcements.post("mymod_boss", "Steve defeated the Dragon!")` (shown in Discord when
"News from other mods" is on); listen with `Announcements.listen((category, text) -> ...)`.


# Rewards, mail and boosts

Item and command rewards, the mailbox, boosts for a while and rank perks.

## Item and command rewards: `Rewards` (API version 18)

The same rewards in every plugin. Admins type items as one line (`Ingredient_Bar_Iron x16, Food_Bread x5`; `16
Food_Bread` and a bare id for one work too), at most `Rewards.MAX_KINDS` (8) kinds and `MAX_AMOUNT` (1000) of each.
`giveItems` puts them in the inventory; what does not fit, and everything for a player who is offline, waits in the
mailbox. The parcel is saved before anything is given, so a crash can neither lose nor double it. Any thread.

```java
if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 18) {
    String problem = Rewards.itemsProblem(text);              // in the editor: null when it can be saved
    List<Mailbox.Item> items = Rewards.parseItems(text);      // the same ids added together, junk left out
    Rewards.describe(items);                                  // "16 Ingredient Bar Iron, 5 Food Bread", for players
    Rewards.giveItems(uuid, "Dragons", "server.dragons.mail.reward", Map.of("dragon", "Ember"), items);
    Rewards.commandProblem(command);                          // one line, at most MAX_COMMAND (200) characters
    Rewards.runCommand(uuid, name, "cratekey give {player} vote 1");   // as the console; name null: looked up online
}
```


## One mailbox for every plugin: `Mailbox` (API version 6)

Instead of dropping a reward at a player's feet (full inventory) or keeping it in your own file until they come back
(offline), send it to their mailbox. Players open it with `/mail`, are told when a parcel arrives and when they join,
and see "Mail: 2" on the Tempest board. Claiming gives what fits; the rest stays in the parcel, and money is paid
through the server's economy.

```java
if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 6) {
    String id = Mailbox.send(uuid, "Dragons", "server.dragons.mail.reward",
            Map.of("dragon", "%server.dragons.name.ember"),          // a value starting with % is a translation key
            List.of(new Mailbox.Item("Rock_Gem_Ruby", 3)), 500);   // items and money
    if (id == null) { ... }   // nothing in it, or the mailbox is full (Mailbox.MAX_PARCELS): keep the reward yourself
}
Mailbox.count(uuid);   Mailbox.of(uuid);   // what is waiting
```

The title is a key in your plugin's `server.lang`, so each player reads it in their language. Crates sends keys from
`/cratekey` and key parties there when the player is not in a world.


## Boosts for a while: `Boosts` (API version 5)

More of something for a while: monster and ore gold, daily and quest rewards, battle pass XP, shop prices. Tempest
Events turns them on during an event; your plugin can too (a full moon, a boss kill, a vote party). The plugins that pay
out ask for the boost at the moment they pay, in percent like `Perks` (100 = double). Several sources add up, to at
most 1000%; a discount takes at most 90% off.

```java
core.boost("mymod:full-moon", (kind, player) -> Boosts.MOB_COINS.equals(kind) && fullMoon() ? 50 : 0);   // Registrations
long paid = Boosts.boosted(Boosts.MOB_COINS, killer, amount);   // what Coins does for each monster
long price = Boosts.discounted(Boosts.SHOP_DISCOUNT, player, price);
Boosts.percent(Boosts.PASS_XP, player);                         // 50.0
```

| Kind | Used by | What it raises |
|---|---|---|
| `MOB_COINS` | Coins | coins a monster drops (after the admin's cap) |
| `ORE_COINS` | Coins | coins found in ores |
| `DAILY_REWARD` | Coins | the daily reward (after rank perks) |
| `QUEST_REWARD` | Quests | quest and achievement rewards (after rank perks) |
| `PASS_XP` | Pass | battle pass XP (added to the Pro weekend boost) |
| `SHOP_SELL` | Shop | what the shop pays (never more than its buying price) |
| `SHOP_DISCOUNT` | Shop | off the shop's prices |
| `"contract_pay"` | Contracts | what server orders pay (players' contracts pay what their poster put up, never boosted) |

Your own kind: pay out through `Boosts.boosted("mymod_bounty", player, amount)` and describe it with
`Boosts.describe("mymod_bounty", Message.translation("server.mymod.boost"), "Weapon_Sword_Iron")`, so Tempest Events'
editor lists it and admins can boost it in their events. Games of chance (slots, lottery, coinflip) are never boosted:
it would change the odds players were shown.

A plugin built against Core 1.0.x and run with an older Core must not touch `Boosts`; check first:
`if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 5) { ... }`.

Personal boosters need no code: `/booster <player> <kind> <percent> <minutes>` (permission `tempest.boosters`, also
from the console) gives one player a boost of any described kind for a while, so a crate's command prize, a quest or a
vote plugin can hand them out. They count like any other source and show under the coin counter with the time left.
`/booster <player> clear 0 0` takes them away.


## Rank perks: `Perks`

Admins set up to four perks in `/tempest` (Rank Perks tab), each tied to a permission such as `coins.perk.vip`, which a
permissions plugin gives to a rank. Read them for your own rewards:

```java
Perks.percent(uuid, Perks.Bonus.DAILY_REWARD);            // 25.0 = 25% more
Perks.boosted(uuid, Perks.Bonus.QUEST_REWARD, 100);       // 125
Perks.discounted(uuid, Perks.Bonus.SHOP_DISCOUNT, 100);   // 90
Perks.name(uuid);                                         // "VIP", or "" without a perk
```

Perks are checked against the player's permissions while they are online; offline players get none.

`Perks.highestPercent(Perks.Bonus.SHOP_DISCOUNT)` (API version 9) is the best value any perk on the server gives,
whoever has it. Cap what you pay players with it, so someone with a discount cannot buy for a friend who sells back.

`Perks.Bonus.PASS_XP` (API version 10) is a rank's pass XP bonus; Tempest Pass (Pro) adds it to every XP gain.
Check `CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 10` before using it.


# Map, town and demand

Places on the world map, features the town unlocks and items the server wants.

## Places on the world map: `MapPlaces` (API version 7)

Register a kind of place and Core does the rest: a tab in `/tempest` (on or off, icon, colour, name, size, compass, who
sees it, how far away, which worlds), changing or hiding one place from `/places`, and each player picking what their
map shows.

```java
// Blocks: Core remembers each one when it is placed or used, and forgets it when it goes
core.mapKind(new MapPlaces.Kind("nest", "Dragon nests", Message.translation("server.dragons.map.nest"))
        .icon("Tempest_Star.png").color("#E74C3C").item("Rock_Gem_Ruby")
        .blocks(id -> id.equals("Dragon_Nest")));

// Or your own list, asked for every few seconds on any thread, so keep it quick
core.mapKind(new MapPlaces.Kind("dragon", "Dragons", Message.translation("server.dragons.map.dragon"))
        .places(() -> dragons.stream()
                .map(d -> new MapPlaces.Place(d.id(), d.world(), d.x(), d.y(), d.z(), d.name())).toList()));

MapPlaces.refresh();   // after a change that should show at once
```

`Kind.startOff()` leaves a kind off until an admin turns it on. A place's `key` must stay the same, as admins' changes
are kept under it. The second argument of `Kind` is what admins read in `/tempest`; the third is what players read.
Icons are files in `Common/UI/WorldMap/MapMarkers`, so an asset pack can add its own: `MapPlaces.ICONS` lists what every
server has. Paint them white with a dark edge and the admin's colour tints them.


## Features the town unlocks: `Unlocks` (API version 8)

Some features should wait until the server has earned them: savings interest once the town has a bank, market stalls
once the market hall stands. Describe each such feature, and ask Core before using it:

```java
core.unlockFeature(new Unlocks.Feature("dragons:nest_rewards", "Dragon nest rewards",       // Registrations
        Message.translation("server.dragons.unlock.nests"), "Rock_Gem_Ruby"));
if (Unlocks.isOn("dragons:nest_rewards")) { payNestReward(); }
core.onUnlock((feature, on) -> { if (feature.equals("dragons:nest_rewards")) refreshNests(); });
```

- The id is your plugin's name and the feature; keep it the same, as admins' choices are kept under it. The second
  argument is what admins read in menus, the third what players read on `/town`.
- **Without a provider every feature is on**, so a server without Tempest Town works as before and your plugin's own
  settings decide. Tempest Town is the provider (`tempest:town`): an admin ties features to unlocks there (always on,
  always off, or once a building is finished, a date has come or another unlock came first). A feature no unlock names
  stays on.
- `isOn` is asked from any thread and answers from memory, so call it as often as you like. A listener hears a feature
  switched on or off on the thread that changed it.
- Your own provider (a plugin that decides unlocks some other way): `core.unlockProvider("mymod", feature -> ...)`
  returns `TRUE`, `FALSE`, or `null` to leave the feature on. A feature is off when any provider says off. Tell the
  plugins with `Unlocks.fire(feature, on)` when your answer changes.
- `Unlocks.features()` lists every described feature (Town's editor shows them); check `CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 8`
  first when your plugin may run with an older Core.


## Items the server wants: `Demand` (Core, API version 17)

A plugin with orders tells Core what is wanted; any plugin asks Core, so neither depends on the other. Tempest
Contracts provides the items of its open server orders (players' own contracts do not count, so a cheap one cannot
raise everyone's pay); Tempest Jobs pays more for work that brings one in.

```java
core.demandSource("myplugin", () -> Set.of("Ore_Iron", "Wood_Oak_Trunk"));   // removed by core.close()
Demand.isWanted("Ore_Iron_Stone");   // true: the id contains a wanted id ("_Item" endings are ignored)
Demand.wanted();                     // every wanted id now, from every source (kept for 10 seconds)
```


# Safety and helpers

Admin logs, rate limits, play limits, AFK checks, the doctor and crash-safe files.

## Who changed what: `AdminLog` (API version 2)

Record admin changes so servers with several staff can see who did what. Lines go to
`universe/mods/atomictempest/admin-log/<day>.log`; `/tempest log` shows the newest. Line breaks in the text are
removed, so a typed name cannot add a false line.

```java
AdminLog.record(player.getUsername(), "Dragons", "Bounty: 250 -> 500");
AdminLog.record(AdminLog.CONSOLE, "Dragons", "Reset every dragon");
```


## Stopping floods: `RateLimit` (API version 2)

At most once in a while per key, for announcements, payments and messages a player could repeat:

```java
if (RateLimit.allow("dragons:announce:" + player, 30_000)) { announce(...); }
```


## A daily limit for games of chance: `PlayLimits` (API version 3)

The admin sets one daily limit per player for every game of chance together (`/tempest`, General, "Daily limit for
games"; 0 = none). A game counts each stake before it takes the money, and gives it back if the money is not taken
or the stake is refunded:

```java
Message stop = PlayLimits.reserve(player, bet);   // counts the bet, or says why not (shown to the player)
if (stop != null) { player.sendMessage(stop); return; }
if (!economy.withdraw(player, bet, "Dragon dice")) { PlayLimits.release(player, bet); return; }
```

`PlayLimits.check(player, amount)` says why without counting (for a price shown before buying);
`PlayLimits.leftToday(player)` is what the player may still stake today.


## Who is really playing: `Activity` (API version 9)

Pay for time played only to players who are there. A player counts as active while they turned their view in the last
`Activity.AFK_MINUTES` (5) minutes; water pushing them or standing in a farm moves them but never turns their head.
A player who has just joined counts as active.

```java
if (Activity.isActive(uuid)) { addMinutePlayed(uuid); }
Activity.idleMillis(uuid);   // how long they have not turned their view
```

Tempest Pass (minutes played) and Tempest Events (playtime goals) use it. Check `CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 9` first.


## Catching money from nothing: `Doctor` (API version 13)

`/tempest doctor` looks through every plugin's settings for ways players could make money from nothing, before they
find them. A plugin that pays coins or takes items for coins adds a check, and its prices take part in every check the
doctor runs across plugins:

```java
core.doctor(new Doctor.Check() {                                     // Registrations
    public void prices(Doctor.Market market) {
        // where players buy items for coins, and get coins for items, with the settings as they are now
        market.buy("my stall", "Ingredient_Bar_Iron", 12, 0, "/mystall");        // 0 = no daily limit
        market.sell("my bounty board", "Ingredient_Bar_Iron", 20, 64, "/bounties");
        market.play(Doctor.CRATE_OPENS, averageLossPerOpening, "my crate");    // for quests that count openings
    }
    public void check(Doctor.Market market, Doctor.Findings findings) {
        long worth = market.worth("Rock_Gem_Diamond");                // the most any plugin pays for one
        if (myPrize > myPrice) findings.problem("prize", "My prize is worth more than it costs.", "My price");
    }
});
```

Core itself finds every item bought cheaper in one place than it sells for in another, and every game recipe whose
parts, bought at their cheapest, cost less than what it makes sells for (items only admins may craft are left out).
A finding is `problem` (money from nothing), `warning` (easy to farm) or `hint`. Its key must stay the same between
checks, as the admin can mark it "on purpose". A fix is a command (`"/shop"`) or the label of a setting in /tempest,
which the FIX button searches for. Texts are for admins and may be English. Give the most a player can get (rank perks
and running `Boosts` included): the doctor is there for the worst case. `new Doctor.Findings(list)` collects findings in a
plugin's own tests. Check `CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 13` first, and keep the check in a class of its own.


## Saving files safely: `SafeFiles`

All six plugins save through it, and other plugins may too. A save survives a crash or power cut at any moment:
the text goes to `name.tmp` (flushed to disk), the old file becomes `name.bak`, then the new one takes its place.

```java
SafeFiles.write(path, gson.toJson(data));                          // throws IOException if it could not save
MyData data = SafeFiles.load(path, reader -> gson.fromJson(reader, MyData.class));  // null if no copy can be read
SafeFiles.exists(path);                                            // also true if only the .tmp or .bak is left
```

`load` uses the newest complete copy; a file that cannot be read is kept as `name.broken-<time>` and the backup is
used instead.


## Other helpers

- `Currency`: the money's name (`format`, `name`, `singular`, `plural`). Use it instead of writing "copper".
- `ChatPrefix.of(text, "#RRGGBB")`: a coloured chat tag such as "[Dragons]".
- `ItemIcons.safe(itemId)`: an item id that is safe to draw; Coins' coin items fall back to similar game items when
  Coins is not installed.
- `CoinStacks.of(amount)` (in Coins): the coin items that make up an amount (for dropping coins).
- `ReservedDrops.spawn(...)`: dropped items only one player can pick up for a while.
- `CraftRestrictions.restrict(itemId, () -> allowed)`: admin-only crafting with an on/off switch.


# Player levels

Levels from Endless Leveling or MMO Skill Tree, through one API.

## Player levels: `Levels` (API version 14)

Player levels from whichever leveling mod the server runs, as `Economies` is for money: **Endless Leveling** or **MMO
Skill Tree**, found by themselves through their public APIs (nothing of them is shipped). With both installed, the admin
picks the one that gives "the level" on the /tempest Leveling tab. Another mod's bridge can `Levels.register` its own
`Leveling`, which then comes first.

```java
Levels.Leveling leveling = Levels.get();            // null without a leveling mod
if (leveling != null) {
    int level = leveling.level(uuid);
    int prestige = leveling.prestige(uuid);          // 0 with MMO Skill Tree
    leveling.giveXp(uuid, 250, "Quest: Miner");      // with the mod's own bonuses and level cap
}
if (!Levels.meets(uuid, 20)) { ... }                 // true without a leveling mod: nobody is locked out by a missing mod
```

> **Note:** With MMO Skill Tree, `level` is the number the admin chose on its tab (total, combat or power level, or the
> highest skill), and leveling XP goes into the skill chosen there. Its skills one by one are in `Skills` (below).

### `Levels` (static)

| Method | Returns | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get()` | `Leveling` | 14 | The leveling mod in use, or null. Asked again on every call |
| `register(leveling)` / `unregister(leveling)` | | 14 | A bridge for another leveling mod; it is preferred over the ones Core finds |
| `listen(listener)` / `stopListening(listener)` | | 14 | Hear level-ups, prestige and clears (below) |
| `available()` | `boolean` | 16 | A leveling mod runs |
| `level(uuid)` | `int` | 16 | The player's level, 0 without a leveling mod |
| `meets(uuid, minLevel)` | `boolean` | 16 | The player has at least this level; true without a leveling mod |
| `hasClass(uuid, wanted)` | `boolean` | 16 | The player's class (or second class) is this one; true without a mod or a class |
| `mobLevel(ref, store, buffer)` | `int` | 16 | A mob's level (Endless Leveling), 0 when not known. On the mob's world thread |
| `mobGold(amount, killer, mobLevel)` | `long` | 16 | Mob gold raised by the mob's level, as the admin set it |
| `mobKilled(killer, mobName, mobLevel)` | | 16 | Tell Core of a kill (elite mob announcements) |
| `playersAtLevel(level)` | `int` | 16 | Players seen at this level or higher (for town conditions) |
| `serverClears()` / `serverPrestige()` | `long` | 16 | Dungeons, gates and raids cleared by everyone; everyone's highest prestige added up |
| `pretty(id)` | `String` | 16 | "dark_knight" becomes "Dark Knight" |
| `describe()` | `String` | 14 | "Endless Leveling", "MMO Skill Tree" or "none" |
| `fireLevelUp`, `firePrestige`, `fireDungeonCleared`, `fireGateCleared`, `fireRaidCleared`, `fireRaidStarted` | | 14-16 | For a bridge: tell Core and every listener |

### `Levels.Leveling` (one leveling mod)

| Method | Returns | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name()` | `String` | 14 | "Endless Leveling", "MMO Skill Tree" |
| `level(uuid)` / `prestige(uuid)` | `int` | 14 | Level and prestige (0 when the mod does not know the player) |
| `giveXp(uuid, amount, reason)` | `boolean` | 14 | XP with the mod's bonuses and cap; false when it could not |
| `xp(uuid)` / `xpForNext(uuid)` | `double` | 16 | XP toward the next level, and what it needs (0 when the mod does not say) |
| `levelCap(uuid)` | `int` | 16 | The highest level this player can reach (0: not said) |
| `playerClass(uuid)` / `secondClass(uuid)` / `race(uuid)` | `String` | 16 | Class, second class and race ids ("mage"), "" for none |
| `mobLevel(ref, store, buffer)` | `int` | 16 | A mob's level, on its world thread |
| `inPartyWith(one, other)` | `boolean` | 16 | The two players are in one party |

### `Levels.Listener` events

All default methods: override what you need. They run on the thread the leveling mod fires on, so keep them quick.

| Event | Fires when | Carries | Since |
|---|---|---|---|
| `levelUp` | A player's level went up (once, even when several levels were crossed) | player, oldLevel, newLevel | 14 |
| `prestige` | A player prestiged (Endless Leveling) | player, oldPrestige, newPrestige | 14 |
| `dungeonCleared` | A dungeon the player was in was cleared | player, rank ("E" to "S", "" without) | 15 |
| `gateCleared` | A wave gate or fate zone the player fought in was cleared | player, rank, waves | 15 |
| `raidCleared` | The player finished a raid | player, waves | 15 |
| `raidStarted` | A raid started for everyone | name, world, waves | 16 |

```java
Levels.listen(new Levels.Listener() {                  // stopListening in shutdown (or Registrations.onClose)
    @Override
    public void levelUp(UUID player, int oldLevel, int newLevel) { ... }
    @Override
    public void dungeonCleared(UUID player, String rank) { ... }
});
```

> **Note:** With both mods installed only the chosen mod's level-ups and prestige reach listeners, so nothing counts
> twice. Endless Leveling's dungeons, gates and raids are told either way: only it has them.

### What Core does with it, and tabs for your plugin

Core pays the admin's money per level-up (with a bonus at milestones), gives the placeholders `{leveling_level}`,
`{leveling_prestige}`, `{leveling_xp}` and more, raises rewards by level (the level bonus), and shows a "Highest levels"
board while a leveling mod runs. Its settings are on three /tempest tabs: **Leveling** (with either mod), **Endless
Leveling** (only while it runs: prestige, dungeons, gates, raids, mob gold by level, elite mobs) and **MMO Skill Tree**
(only while it runs).

| Method | Since | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Registrations.levelingTab(tab)` | 16 | A /tempest tab shown only while a leveling mod runs |
| `Registrations.endlessTab(tab)` | 19 | A tab shown only while Endless Leveling runs (for what only it has) |
| `Registrations.levelingFeature(feature)` | 16 | A town unlock feature offered only while a leveling mod runs |

`Boosts.LEVELING_XP` (15) raises leveling XP: Core gives the extra through the mod each time it gives a player XP
(Endless Leveling, or MMO Skill Tree in the same skill), so Tempest Events, rank perks and boosters can run "double
leveling XP". With both mods installed it raises both. The extra is never boosted again.


# Skills (MMO Skill Tree)

Skill levels, skill XP, achievements, quests and NPC talks.

## Skills: `Skills` (Core, API version 19)

MMO Skill Tree's skills, while it runs: one level per skill (Mining, Swords, custom skills too), skill XP, and what
happens there. Found by itself, nothing of it is shipped. Works next to Endless Leveling: skills are MMO Skill Tree's
own, whichever mod gives "the level".

```java
if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 19 && Skills.available()) {
    int mining = Skills.level(player, "Mining");        // by id or name; 0 when not known yet
    Map<String, Integer> all = Skills.levels(player);   // "MINING" -> 34, ...
    Skills.giveXp(player, "Mining", 500, "My mod: a task");   // blank skill: the one the admin chose in Core
}
```

| Method | Returns | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `available()` | `boolean` | MMO Skill Tree runs |
| `ids()` | `List<String>` | The server's skill ids, custom ones too ("MINING", "HERBALISM") |
| `name(id)` | `String` | The skill's name for players ("Mining") |
| `find(typed)` | `String` | The id a typed name or id stands for ("light armor" gives "LIGHT_ARMOR"), "" for none |
| `subject(id)` | `String` | "MINING Mining": the id and name, as in the actions below |
| `levels(uuid)` | `Map<String, Integer>` | Every skill's level, as last read; empty when not known |
| `level(uuid, skill)` | `int` | One skill's level (id or name), 0 when not known |
| `giveXp(uuid, skill, amount, reason)` | `boolean` | Skill XP with the mod's XP banner; false when the mod is not running or the player is offline |

### Its moments, as `PlayerActions`

What players do there is fired as `PlayerActions`, with the skill, achievement, quest or character after the colon.
Tempest Quests counts them as goals; any plugin can.

| Action (prefix constant) | Fires when | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| `mmo_skill_level:<id> <name>` (`Skills.SKILL_LEVEL`) | A skill's level went up | The new level |
| `mmo_skill_xp:<id> <name>` (`Skills.SKILL_XP`) | XP from play (not XP Tempest gave) | The XP |
| `mmo_achievement:<id>` (`Skills.ACHIEVEMENT`) | An achievement was unlocked | 1 |
| `mmo_quest:<id>` (`Skills.QUEST`) | One of its own quests was finished | 1 |
| `npc_talk:<character id> <aliases>` (`Skills.NPC_TALK`) | A credited conversation with a character | 1 |

```java
PlayerActions.listen((player, action, amount) -> {
    if (action.startsWith(Skills.SKILL_LEVEL)) {
        String skill = action.substring(Skills.SKILL_LEVEL.length());   // "MINING Mining"
        // ...
    }
});
```

> **Note:** Levels are read when a player joins, every half minute and after every XP gain; a player who has just
> joined may have none for a moment. Core pays its own skill-level and achievement rewards (the MMO Skill Tree tab),
> each level and each achievement once ever.


# Leveling mods for server owners

What the Tempest plugins do with Endless Leveling and MMO Skill Tree, alone or together, and where it is set.

Tempest works with **Endless Leveling** (by Airijko) and **MMO Skill Tree** (by Ziggfreed). Nothing of either mod
is shipped: Tempest Core finds them through their public APIs within half a minute of the server starting. Without
them, nothing changes, and no level requirement ever locks a player out because a mod is missing.

## One mod, or both

| Installed | What happens |
|---|---|
| Endless Leveling only | Its level counts for everything below; its prestige, dungeons, wave gates, raids, classes and mob levels work too |
| MMO Skill Tree only | Its skills become one level (total, combat, power level or the highest skill, as you choose); skill and achievement rewards work too |
| Both | You choose whose level counts ("Leveling mod" on the Leveling tab). Only that mod's level-ups pay level-up money, so nothing is paid twice. Endless Leveling's dungeons, gates and raids and MMO Skill Tree's skill and achievement rewards keep working. "Double leveling XP" raises both |

## Where to set it: `/tempest`

Every amount starts at 0, which is off: installing a mod changes nothing until you choose.

| Tab | Shown | What is on it |
|---|---|---|
| Leveling | With either mod | Which mod counts (with "In use: ..."), money per level-up and milestones, the level bonus on other rewards, chat lines, boards, XP boosts |
| Leveling extras | With either mod | Commands at levels, leveling XP from the economy (daily rewards, crates, contracts, the shop, town projects), levels for paying and gambling (stops alts), town bonuses |
| Endless Leveling | Only with Endless Leveling | Prestige (money, a command, a bonus), dungeon, gate and raid money, mob gold by mob level, elite mobs |
| MMO Skill Tree | Only with MMO Skill Tree | Which number is "the level", which skill gets Tempest's XP, money and items per skill level and at milestones, achievement and server-first rewards |
| Pass leveling, PvP leveling, Events leveling | With their plugin | Pass XP for level-ups (and Endless Leveling clears), PvP rewards by level, events that start with raids (Endless Leveling) |

## What players get

| Plugin | With a leveling mod |
|---|---|
| Core | Money for level-ups, commands and items at levels, a bonus on other rewards by level, placeholders and a "Highest levels" board |
| Quests | Goals: reach a level; with Endless Leveling also prestige, dungeons, gates, raids and strong mobs; with MMO Skill Tree reach a skill level, gain skill XP, earn achievements, finish its quests, talk to characters. Rewards can give leveling XP (a goal about one skill gives that skill's XP) |
| Shop, Crates, Quests | Items, crates and quests that need a level (and with Endless Leveling a class) |
| Pass | Pass XP for level-ups; tiers can give leveling XP |
| Jobs | Job work gives leveling XP; a job can need a level |
| Contracts | PvP rewards for underdogs and fines for bullies, by level |
| Events | "Double leveling XP" events; with Endless Leveling community goals for dungeons, gates and raids |

## MMO Skill Tree rewards

| Reward | How it works |
|---|---|
| Money per skill level | Paid for every level gained in a skill, more at higher levels; only above the highest level ever paid, so a reset pays nothing again |
| Skill milestones | A bonus, items (what does not fit goes to `/mail`) and a line for everyone every so many levels |
| Only these skills | Limit the rewards to the skills you list |
| Achievements | Money per achievement and per achievement point, once each |
| Server firsts | A bonus, items and a line for everyone for an achievement only the first player can earn |

Placeholders: `{leveling_level}` (the level that counts), `{mmo_total_level}`, `{mmo_combat_level}`, `{mmo_power}`.

> **Note:** MMO Skill Tree reads a player when they join, every half minute and after every XP gain. A player who has
> just joined may show no level for a moment.


# Quests

Your own kinds of goals, goals shipped with your mod, progress and custom triggers.

## Quests: `QuestsAPI`

### Your own kind of goal

```java
// setup(): admins can now pick "Catch fish" in the editor (/quests, Edit tab)
QuestsAPI.registerObjective("fishing:catch", "Catch fish", "Catch", "fish", true,
        "Fish id or part of it, e.g. Salmon. Empty: any fish.");

// whenever a player catches a fish
QuestsAPI.progress(playerUuid, "fishing:catch", fishItemId, 1);
```

Goals made with it are kept while your mod is not installed, but they do not count. You can also count the
built-in kinds yourself, for example `QuestsAPI.progress(uuid, "KILL", "Dragon", 1)` for a mob the game does not
report.

### Shipping goals with your mod

```java
QuestsAPI.addGoal(GoalInfo.achievement("fishing:first_catch", "First catch", "Food_Fish_Raw",
        "fishing:catch", "", 1, 50));
QuestsAPI.addGoal(GoalInfo.quest("fishing:daily", "Daily angler", "Food_Fish_Raw",
        "fishing:catch", "", 10, 80, "daily"));
```

`addGoal` does nothing if a goal with that id exists, so it is safe on every start and keeps the admin's changes.

### Reading progress and hearing about it

```java
QuestsAPI.isDone(uuid, "fishing:first_catch");
QuestsAPI.progressOf(uuid, "fishing:daily");
QuestsAPI.goals();                                  // every goal, as GoalInfo
QuestsAPI.onComplete((uuid, goal) -> { ... });      // after the reward was paid
QuestsAPI.givesPassXp(goal.id());                   // version 2: false when the admin switched pass XP off for it
```

`givesPassXp` is new in `QuestsAPI.API_VERSION` 2; against an older Quests catch `NoSuchMethodError` and treat it as
true.

### Custom triggers (no new objective needed)

Admins can make a goal of the kind **Custom trigger** and type a name in "Which one", for example `visit_shrine`.
It counts whenever that trigger fires, from any of these:

- Java: `QuestsAPI.trigger(uuid, "visit_shrine", 1)`
- A command (console, admins, other plugins): `/questtrigger <player> visit_shrine 1` (permission `quests.admin`)
- A content mod's item, block or NPC: the `Quests_Trigger` interaction (below)


# Crates

## Crates

Crates are made by admins in game (`/crates`, Edit crates, permission `crates.admin`) and saved in
`universe/mods/crates/crates.json`. Each opening is reported as `PlayerActions.CRATE_OPEN` (amount: the price), which
the Quests mod counts for "Open crates" goals; prizes rarer than the admin's threshold are posted to
`Announcements.BIG_WIN`. The price is taken (and can be vetoed) before the prize is drawn.

- Keys: a crate can need `keyAmount` of an item (`keyItem`), usually `Crate_Key_Bronze`, `Crate_Key_Silver` or
  `Crate_Key_Gold`. Give them from other plugins or the console with `/cratekey <player> <bronze|silver|gold|item id>
  <amount>` (permission `crates.admin`); right-clicking a key opens `/crates` (page id `Crates_Page`).
- A crate can be locked to a permission (`permission`, such as `crates.vip`).
- Prizes can be a permission or a permissions group ("rank"), for some days or for good, given through the server's
  `PermissionsModule` and taken back when they run out (unless the player already had them), or a console command
  with `{player}` and `{uuid}`.

- Crate blocks (`Crate_Block_Wooden`, `Crate_Block_Iron`, `Crate_Block_Golden`): which crate each one opens is in
  `universe/mods/crates/places.json` (with each crate's last Rare or better win). Admins set it by right-clicking the
  block (crouch + right-click to change it). The text, circling prizes and floating prizes of openings over them use
  Holograms (below), which is optional for Crates: without it the lid, sparkles and sounds still play. To use Holograms as an
  optional dependency, touch its classes in one class of yours only, after checking that they exist.


# Holograms

Floating text, items, statues and rankings.

## Holograms: `Holograms` (Holograms plugin)

Floating text, coloured text pictures, floating show-only items and player statues, from any plugin (`Holograms.API_VERSION`, 3). Holograms placed through this
API have no limit in either edition; the free edition limits only the ones admins place with `/holo`. Add `"AtomicTempest:Holograms": "*"` to your manifest's
dependencies (or `OptionalDependencies`, as Crates does) and compile against the Holograms jar (the Maven repository above, `compileOnly`).

```java
Hologram sign = Holograms.text("myplugin", world, new Vector3d(10.5, 66, 4.5),
        List.of(Message.raw("Welcome!"), Message.translation("server.myplugin.sign.hint")));
sign.setLines(...);          // players see the new text within a moment
sign.moveTo(...);  sign.remove();
FloatingItem gem = Holograms.item("myplugin", world, position, "Rock_Gem_Ruby");
gem.glow("#FF4060");         // a coloured light on it (null = none)
gem.moveTo(...);             // on the world thread it moves at once: call it every tick to animate
Statue champion = Holograms.statue("myplugin", worldName, feet, playerUuid);   // API_VERSION 2
champion.show(otherUuid);    // another player; null shows nobody
TextImage banner = Holograms.coloured("myplugin", worldName, feet,
        () -> List.of(Message.raw("<gradient:#FF4040:#40C0FF>Welcome</gradient>"), Message.raw("&aShop &7open")));  // API_VERSION 3
banner.setSize(1.5f);  banner.setFacing(false, yaw);   // a fixed yaw instead of facing every player
Holograms.texts();           // every plugin's floating text now (API_VERSION 3; /holo menu lists them)
Colours.strip("&cRed");      // "Red"; Colours.runs(...) splits a line into coloured pieces for menus
Holograms.removeAll("myplugin");   // in shutdown()
```

- Coloured text (API_VERSION 3): `Holograms.coloured` draws the lines into a picture (the game's interface font,
  Nunito Sans, OFL) and hangs it on one flat two-sided model; the picture and model are sent to every player while
  they play, and to each player who joins. Codes: `&c` and the other 15 classic colours, `&#FF8800` or `<#FF8800>`,
  `<red>`..`</red>`, `<gradient:#F00:#00F>text</gradient>`, `<rainbow>text</rainbow>`. Everyone sees the same
  picture: the server's language, placeholders for nobody (server-wide ones work). A changed text is drawn again
  at most every 15 s, and only while a player is near. By default it faces every player at once: each player's copy
  of its turn is rewritten on the way out (the same packet watcher as the languages), 20 times a second while players move. Plain floating text leaves the codes out, since the game draws it in white.

- A statue is a life-size figure of a player as they looked when they last joined (Holograms keeps each player's
  skin in `universe/mods/holograms/skins.json`), turning to face the nearest player. It shows nothing for a player
  Holograms has not seen join. Leaderboard holograms placed with `/holo` can stand their first place on top
  ("Statue of 1st" in the menu).

- Lines are `Message`s: translation keys (with parameters, even nested ones) are shown in each player's language, and
  placeholders (`{lottery_pot}`) are filled in for each player. The game draws it in white; for colours use
  `Holograms.coloured`. The last line is at the position, the others above it (`/tempest` → Holograms sets the spacing).
- Entities exist only while a player is within the view distance and the chunk is loaded; they are never saved and
  vanish by themselves a minute after the plugin stops renewing them. Any thread may call the API.
- How it works: each line is an invisible model (`Server/Models/Holograms_Anchor.json`) with a `Nameplate`; an
  outbound packet watcher swaps the nameplate text in each player's own `EntityUpdates` for their language. Floating
  items are item drops without a `Velocity` (so item physics leave them alone), with `PreventPickup` and
  `PreventItemMerging`.
- Admins place their own with `/holo create|edit|move|delete` or the `/holo menu` page (`holograms.admin`), saved
  in `universe/mods/holograms/holograms.json`.
- Lines worked out again on every refresh (only while a player is near; at most every 5 s):
  `Holograms.live("myplugin", worldName, position, () -> List.of(...))` or `hologram.setSource(...)`. The supplier
  runs on the Holograms timer thread.
- Top lists for leaderboard holograms (`/holo create <name> top:<list> [places]`): Holograms offers Core's
  `Leaderboards` boards and every per-player number placeholder by itself (`top:money`, `top:coins_balance`,
  `top:quests:achievements`), ranking the players it has seen join. A plugin that knows every player (online or
  not) can register its own list:

```java
Rankings.register("mymod_dragons", new Rankings.Ranking() {
    public Message title() { return Message.translation("server.mymod.board.title"); }
    public List<Rankings.Entry> top(int count) { ... new Rankings.Entry(name, Message.raw("12 dragons")) ... }
});
Rankings.unregister("mymod_dragons");   // in shutdown()
```

- Coloured text is not possible with nameplates; `Holograms.coloured` draws pictures instead (above).


# Coinflip

Rooms, and your own kind of room.

## Coinflip: `CoinflipAPI` and `RoomMode` (Coinflip plugin)

Coinflip rooms: a player makes a room with a stake, others join, the coin decides. Add `"AtomicTempest:Coinflip": "*"`
to your manifest's dependencies and compile against the Coinflip jar (the Maven repository above, `compileOnly`).

```java
CoinflipAPI flips = CoinflipAPI.get();               // null while Coinflip is not running
List<Room> open = flips.rooms();                      // open and flipping rooms, oldest first
CoinflipAPI.Result made = flips.create(player, CoinflipAPI.COINS_1V1, Bet.coins(500, Side.HEADS));
if (!made.isOk()) player.sendMessage(made.problem());
flips.join(other, made.room().id(), flips.mode(CoinflipAPI.COINS_1V1).matching(made.room(), other.getUuid()));
flips.cancel(roomId);                                 // every stake goes back; check who asks first
flips.stats(uuid).profit();                           // wins, losses, staked, won
flips.listen(new CoinflipAPI.Listener() {
    public void flipped(Room room) { ... }            // full: winner fixed, coin in the air
    public void finished(Room room) { ... room.winner().name() ... room.payout() ... }
    public void closed(Room room, CoinflipAPI.CloseReason reason) { ... }   // CANCELLED, EXPIRED, RESTART
});
```

- A `Room` has an id, its mode, its `entries()` (player, name, side, value, data; the first made the room), its state
  (`OPEN`, `FLIPPING`, `DONE`, `CLOSED`), `pot()`, `fee()`, `payout()`, `winner()`, and the fairness data: `hash()`
  from the start, `seed()` once the coin has landed, `roll()` once it is full.
- **Provably fair:** the seed is 32 random bytes (hex) from `SecureRandom`; `hash` is SHA-256(seed). The roll is the
  first 13 hex digits of SHA-256(seed + ":" + room id) divided by 16^13 (0 to 1). The mode turns the roll into a
  winner; the coins mode: under 0.5 is heads.
- **Escrow:** stakes are taken when a player makes or joins a room and stay with the room. Open rooms are saved in
  `universe/mods/coinflip/rooms.json`: on the next start (after a stop or a crash) their stakes go back, and a flip
  that was in the air is paid. What cannot be paid or refunded yet (no economy, or the mode's plugin is missing) is
  kept and tried again every few seconds. Stats are in `stats.json`.
- Every flip is reported through `PlayerActions` (`coinflip_bet`, `coinflip_win`, `coinflip_loss`), big wins through
  `Announcements.BIG_WIN`, and profit is a `Leaderboards` board (`coinflip:profit`).

### Your own kind of room: `RoomMode`

Coinflip comes with one mode, `coins_1v1`. A mode decides what players stake, how many play, how the winner is
chosen and how the pot is paid; Coinflip does the rest the same for every mode (the room list, joining and watching,
escrow bookkeeping, the fair roll, the animation, the fee setting, stats, news). Item rooms valued by Shop prices,
jackpot rooms for many players, private invite-only rooms or tournaments are all modes.

```java
public final class JackpotMode implements RoomMode {
    public String id() { return "myplugin_jackpot"; }                 // saved with its rooms
    public Message title() { return Message.translation("server.myplugin.jackpot"); }
    public int maxPlayers() { return 8; }
    public Message describe(Room room) { return Message.raw(Currency.format(room.pot())); }
    public boolean canSee(Room room, UUID viewer) { return true; }    // private rooms: only invited players
    public Bet matching(Room room, UUID joiner) { return Bet.coins(room.creator().value(), null); }  // null: not from the list
    public Taken take(PlayerRef player, Room room, Bet bet) {         // room is null when making a room
        // check the bet, take the stake; nothing may be kept when refused
        return Economies.get().withdraw(player.getUuid(), bet.amount(), "Jackpot stake")
                ? Taken.ok(bet) : Taken.refused(Message.raw("Not enough money"));
    }
    public boolean refund(Room room, Room.Entry entry) {              // false: tried again later
        return Economies.get() != null && Economies.get().deposit(entry.player(), entry.value(), "Jackpot refund");
    }
    public Room.Entry pick(Room room, double roll) { ... }            // weighted by entry.value(), say
    public boolean pay(Room room, Room.Entry winner) {                // false: tried again later
        return Economies.get() != null && Economies.get().deposit(winner.player(), room.payout(), "Jackpot win");
    }
    public boolean full(Room room) { return room.entries().size() >= maxPlayers(); }  // the default
}

CoinflipAPI.get().registerMode(new JackpotMode());   // in setup(); unregisterMode("myplugin_jackpot") in shutdown()
```

- `Bet(amount, side, data)`: `amount` is money (or the worth of what is staked), `side` is null in modes without
  sides, `data` is text for anything else (item ids, an invited player). What `take` returns becomes the entry: its
  amount is the entry's `value()`, used for the pot, stats and news.
- `fee(room, percent)` defaults to the server's fee setting applied to the pot; override it for stakes that are not
  money.
- Every method may be called from any thread, and a player being refunded or paid may be offline. Rooms of a mode
  that is not registered stay saved and are settled once it is registered again.
- The Rooms page lists rooms of every mode (with the mode's title on the row) and lets players join with
  `matching`; `/cf create` and the Create room tab make `coins_1v1` rooms. A mode that needs its own way to make or
  join rooms (choosing items) calls `create` and `join` from its own page or command.


# Jobs

Pay job work from any mod.

## Jobs: `JobsAPI` (Jobs plugin)

Which jobs there are, who holds them and their levels, and a way for any mod to pay job work Jobs cannot see itself
(`JobsAPI.API_VERSION`, 2). Declare `"AtomicTempest:Jobs": "*"` under OptionalDependencies and check
`JobsAPI.get() != null` (null while Jobs is not running).

```java
JobsAPI jobs = JobsAPI.get();
if (jobs != null && jobs.holds(uuid, "miner") && jobs.level(uuid, "miner") >= 10) { ... }
jobs.xp(uuid, "miner"); jobs.earned(uuid, "miner"); jobs.earnedToday(uuid);     // API 2
// A fishing mod's catch, paid to a "fisher" job the admin made: the level bonus, boosts and caps apply
if (jobs != null && JobsAPI.API_VERSION >= 2) {
    jobs.reward(uuid, "fisher", 3, 5);        // false when the player does not hold it; at most 10,000 a call
}
```

Core's `PlayerActions` tells of `jobs_paid` (amount paid), `jobs_level` (the new level), `jobs_tree` (a whole tree
felled, 1) and `jobs_found` (a place found for the first time, 1). Placeholders: `{jobs_list}`, `{jobs_count}`,
`{jobs_earned_today}`, and for each job `{jobs_<id>_level}`, `_xp`, `_percent` (to the next level) and `_earned`.


# Town projects

The buildings players build together, and their states.

## Town projects: `ProjectsAPI` (Projects plugin)

What is being built and how far each building is, and a word whenever a project changes state
(`ProjectsAPI.API_VERSION`, 1). Tempest Town uses it to unlock features when a building is finished. Declare
`"AtomicTempest:Projects": "*"` under OptionalDependencies, keep the classes that touch it in one file of their own
(as Shop does with Holograms), and check `ProjectsAPI.isAvailable()` first.

```java
for (ProjectsAPI.Building b : ProjectsAPI.buildings()) {   // a copy; empty when Projects is not running
    b.id(); b.name(); b.prefab(); b.world(); b.state(); b.percentDone(); b.finished();
}
ProjectsAPI.building("k3f9");          // one, or null
ProjectsAPI.donors("k3f9");            // different players who donated; -1 when there is no such project
ProjectsAPI.listen(listener);          // listener.changed(building): made, paused, finished, stopped, cancelled, removed
ProjectsAPI.stopListening(listener);   // in your shutdown()
```

- `state` is the project's state name: `CLEARING`, `OPEN`, `PAUSED`, `FINISHING`, `FINISHED`, `CANCELLING`, `STOPPING`
  or `STOPPED`. A listener hears `ProjectsAPI.REMOVED` for a project taken off the list (after a cancel has put the old
  ground back, or an admin removed a finished or stopped one).
- `percentDone` is how much of the goal was donated (100 once finished). Donations change no state, so listeners are
  not told about them: read `buildings()` again when you need the numbers.
- Listeners are called on Projects' timer thread, within a second of the change and never while Projects holds a
  lock, so a listener may call `buildings()`. Every call may come from any thread; answers never wait for the builder.
- When Projects stops (or reloads) it forgets every listener: listen again when it is back, or ask `buildings()` on
  a timer, as Town does every minute.


# Battle pass

## Battle pass: `PassAPI` (Pass plugin)

Give pass XP for what players do in your plugin, read their tier, and hear when they reach one
